skill.name: markdown-url
skill.description: Routes suitable public web pages through markdown.new to make their content easier to read, summarize, and quote as Markdown.
skill.summary: Creates markdown.new-prefixed URLs for cleaner Markdown-style page reading.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most static external command and filesystem alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting and URL-scheme rejection. The real issue is intentional routing through markdown.new, which can expose target URLs and page content to a third party. No prompt injection or malicious code execution intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill routes suitable web browsing through markdown.new.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning to avoid private, internal, authenticated, or confidential URLs before using the proxy.

remediation.issue: The helper hardcodes markdown.new as the only proxy target.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external service dependency and provide an opt-out path for users who need direct browsing.

content.value_statement: Web pages can be hard to quote or summarize cleanly. This skill routes suitable URLs through markdown.new for Markdown-friendly page text.
actual_capabilities: Rewrites HTTP and HTTPS URLs to markdown.new-prefixed URLs.
Normalizes bare hostnames to HTTPS before rewriting them.
Guides the agent to use the Markdown view for read-only pages.
Defines block signals such as 401, 403, 429, CAPTCHA, and partial content.
Includes an optional Node.js helper that prints the rewritten URL.
limitations: Target URLs and fetched page content may pass through markdown.new.
It is not suitable for login, OAuth, payment, upload, form, or dashboard workflows.
It does not bypass paywalls, CAPTCHAs, bot detection, or access controls.
The helper rewrites URLs only; it does not fetch or validate page content.

use_cases.title: Summarize public documentation
use_cases.description: Turn public documentation pages into cleaner Markdown input for setup notes and implementation summaries.

use_cases.title: Collect article notes
use_cases.description: Use Markdown-friendly page views to extract key claims, quotes, and citations from public articles.

use_cases.title: Review release notes
use_cases.description: Route changelogs through a readable Markdown view before comparing changes and migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite One URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this URL through markdown.new and return the final browsing URL: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this documentation page through markdown.new when appropriate, then summarize the key setup steps: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Changelogs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use markdown.new for these changelog pages when suitable. Compare breaking changes and migration steps: [URLs].

prompt_templates.title: Extract With Fallback
prompt_templates.prompt: For each source URL, try markdown.new once when appropriate. If blocked, use the original page and note the fallback before extracting evidence: [URLs].

output_examples.input: Rewrite a public documentation page for Markdown reading.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a markdown.new-prefixed URL that keeps the original HTTPS address intact.

output_examples.input: Summarize a public release notes page.
output_examples.output: The response uses the Markdown view for a concise summary and notes any fallback to the original page.
The skill recommends using the original site because authenticated workflows need cookies and interactive behavior.

best_practices: Use the proxy only for public read-only pages.
Fall back to the original URL after the first blocked attempt.
State when markdown.new was used as the content source.
anti_patterns: Routing private, internal, authenticated, payment, or dashboard URLs through the proxy.
Retrying blocked pages repeatedly after access errors or CAPTCHA prompts.
Treating the Markdown view as a full replacement for interactive site behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It rewrites suitable web URLs so the agent can read them through markdown.new as Markdown-friendly pages.

faq.question: Does it fetch pages by itself?
faq.answer: The helper only rewrites URLs. The agent follows the skill instructions to visit the rewritten page when appropriate.

faq.question: Is it safe for private pages?
faq.answer: No. Avoid private, internal, authenticated, or confidential pages because the URL and content may pass through markdown.new.

faq.question: What happens if markdown.new is blocked?
faq.answer: The skill tells the agent to stop retrying and fall back to the original URL.

faq.question: Does it support non-HTTP schemes?
faq.answer: No. The helper rejects other schemes such as mailto and file, and the instructions avoid local paths.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
